Adversarially verify this code-review finding from the M12 diff. Read the actual code (git diff main...HEAD + the file) and try to REFUTE it. Default to isReal=false if it's a false positive, pre-existing, out of scope, or already handled.

Lens: correctness
Severity: low
File: components/customer/UpcomingBookings.tsx (cancel(id) onClick of the Cancel button)
Title: Cancel button cancels irreversibly on a single click with no confirmation
Detail: Clicking "Cancel" calls cancelBooking immediately. The action can charge the full block per the cancellation policy (cancellationOutcome → capture) when a scheduled session is within 1h of start, so an accidental single click can both cancel the booking and charge the customer. A confirmation string `account.cancelConfirm` ("Cancel this booking?") was added to messages/en.json for exactly this but is never used.
Suggestion: Gate the cancel action behind a confirmation (use the existing account.cancelConfirm string via a Dialog/confirm step) before invoking cancelBooking.

content.text:
All facts verified. Let me summarize the verification:

**Verified facts:**
1. `components/customer/UpcomingBookings.tsx:96` — `onClick={() => cancel(item.id)}` calls `cancel()` which immediately invokes `cancelBooking(id)` (line 28-40). No confirmation step.
2. `cancelBooking` (actions.ts:87-100) calls `payments.capture({ amountCents: booking.price_block_cents })` — the **full block** — when `release` is false.
3. `release` is false for a scheduled booking when `cancellationOutcome().action === "charge"`, which per `lib/pricing.ts:130-136` happens when the session start is **less than 1h away** (or already started). So a single accidental click within the 1h window both cancels and charges the full block.
4. `account.cancelConfirm` ("Cancel this booking?") was added in the M12 commit (4430deb) at `messages/en.json:373` and is referenced **nowhere** in the codebase — it was clearly intended for exactly this confirmation gate.
5. A `Dialog` primitive exists at `components/ui/Dialog.tsx` and is not used here. There is no `window.confirm` or any other gating.

**Adversarial considerations (attempts to refute):**
- Is it pre-existing? No — `UpcomingBookings.tsx` and the unused `cancelConfirm` string were both introduced in the M12 diff under review.
- Is it out of scope? No — it's the cancel control added in this very milestone.
- Is it already handled elsewhere? No confirmation exists anywhere in the path; the `disabled={pending}` guard only prevents double-submit, not accidental first click.
- Is the financial impact overstated? No — the capture is the full `price_block_cents`, matching the policy in pricing.ts. The 1h boundary is real.

The only mild nuance is severity: an in-1h accidental cancel is the worst case (charge), but for any booking ≥1h out the click only releases/refunds — still a destructive irreversible action with no undo. The "low" severity is reasonable. The finding is accurate.

input.reason:
Verified against the M12 diff (commit 4430deb) and the source. The finding is accurate on every load-bearing point.

1) No confirmation: In components/customer/UpcomingBookings.tsx the Cancel button (line 96) does `onClick={() => cancel(item.id)}`, and `cancel()` (lines 28-40) calls `cancelBooking(id)` synchronously inside a transition — no Dialog, no window.confirm, no intermediate step. The only guard is `disabled={pending}`, which prevents double-submit, not the accidental first click.

2) Real financial impact: app/(customer)/account/actions.ts `cancelBooking` calls `payments.capture({ amountCents: booking.price_block_cents })` (the full block, lines 94-99) whenever `release` is false. `release` is false for a scheduled booking when `cancellationOutcome().action === "charge"`, which per lib/pricing.ts:130-136 occurs when the session start is less than 1h away (`startMs - nowMs >= ONE_HOUR_MS` is the only release path). So a single accidental click within the 1h window both cancels the booking and charges the full block. For bookings ≥1h out it instead refunds/releases — still an irreversible destructive action with no undo.

3) Unused string: `account.cancelConfirm` = "Cancel this booking?" was added in this same M12 commit at messages/en.json:373 and is referenced nowhere in the codebase (grep across all .ts/.tsx finds zero usages) — clearly intended for this exact confirmation gate.

Adversarial checks failed to refute: not pre-existing (the component and the unused string are both new in M12), not out of scope (it's the cancel control added in this milestone), not handled elsewhere (a Dialog primitive exists at components/ui/Dialog.tsx but is unused here; no confirm path anywhere). Severity "low" is fair since the charge only triggers inside the 1h window, but the destructive-on-single-click behavior plus the dangling intended-but-unused confirm string makes this a genuine correctness/UX defect with a concrete, ready fix.
